messages.author: 807b1956560c3f8f
messages.subject: News from pyStan 2.0.1 and windows
parts:
Hello,

I could compile also version 2.0.1 but only with a python Enthought distribution. I could not do it with other distributions of python :-/
I have a 32 bits distribution of python and I use pyMC, and as it works, I prefer just now not to explore the option of 64 bits as I do not use huge amount of data (in general). But I guess it will work the same with 64 bits distributions of python. Now, recently, I think the Enthought 64 bits distribution of python is free (some months ago it wasn't)...

You can locate the exe file here:

https://dl.dropboxusercontent.com/u/21286756/pystan-2.0.1.0.win32-py2.7.exe

But I'm afraid the example of schools does not run: problems of memory:

 File "C:\Python27\lib\site-packages\pystan\api.py", line 12, in <module>
    import pystan._api  # stanc wrapper
ImportError: DLL load failed: Invalid access to memory location.

The code is as usual (I think):

mport pystan
import numpy as np

schools_code = """
data {
    int<lower=0> J; // number of schools
    real y[J]; // estimated treatment effects
    real<lower=0> sigma[J]; // s.e. of effect estimates
}
parameters {
    real mu;
    real<lower=0> tau;
    real eta[J];
}
transformed parameters {
    real theta[J];
    for (j in 1:J)
        theta[j] <- mu + tau * eta[j];
}
model {
    eta ~ normal(0, 1);
    y ~ normal(theta, sigma);
}
"""

schools_dat = {'J': 8,
               'y': [28,  8, -3,  7, -1,  1, 18, 12],
               'sigma': [15, 10, 16, 11,  9, 11, 10, 18]}

fit = pystan.stan(model_code=schools_code, data=schools_dat,
                  iter=1000, chains=4)

print(fit)

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] News from pyStan 2.0.1 and windows
parts:
Hi Juan,

Thanks for your efforts.

My sense is that there might be a compiler issue here. I gather the same
compiler needs to be used to compile the Python extension as was used to compile
Python itself. (Perhaps this isn't true?)

Somewhere there is a Cython/Windows expert who will sort this all out, I hope.

Best,

Allen
